nisbett-wilson-1977.title: Richard E. Nisbett and Timothy DeCamp Wilson, "Telling More Than We Can Know: Verbal Reports on Mental Processes," Psychological Review 84(3), May 1977, pp. 231-259

consulted.copy: Scanned journal pages hosted at https://web.math.princeton.edu/~sswang/literature_general_unsorted/Nisbett-Wilson-PsychologicalReview1977.pdf, rendered to images and read page by page

nisbett-wilson-1977.notes: Primary source for the stocking/nightgown position effect, the review of Maier (1931), the observer comparison (including Latane and Darley 1970), a priori causal theories, the content/process distinction, and the inadequate-feedback argument.

johansson-et-al-2005.title: Petter Johansson, Lars Hall, Sverker Sikstrom, and Andreas Olsson, "Failure to Detect Mismatches Between Intention and Outcome in a Simple Decision Task," Science 310(5745), 2005, pp. 116-119

consulted.copy: Abstract and bibliographic record in the Lund University Publications repository

johansson-et-al-2005.notes: Only the abstract was read. Detection rates and procedural detail beyond the abstract are not verified against the article; see choice-blindness-secondary.

choice-blindness-secondary.title: Secondary reports of Johansson et al. (2005): Lund University press release via ScienceDaily (7 October 2005), and Hall, Johansson, Tarning, Sikstrom and Deutgen (2010), Cognition 117(1), pp. 54-61

consulted.copy: Search-result excerpts only; neither document was read in full

choice-blindness-secondary.notes: Excerpts state that fewer than 10% of manipulations were detected immediately and no more than about a fifth to a quarter in total. The lecture therefore says only that most switched trials went unnoticed. Upgrade to the full Science article when available.

lindsey-2025-biology.title: Jack Lindsey et al. (Anthropic), "On the Biology of a Large Language Model," Transformer Circuits Thread, 27 March 2025

consulted.copy: Web page; the Introduction and the section "Addition" were read

lindsey-2025-biology.notes: Studies Claude 3.5 Haiku (October 2024 release). The Addition section gives the 36+59 parallel pathways, the model's carry-the-one explanation, and the interpretation about lacking metacognitive insight. Model output and the interpretive sentence are quoted from this section. The lead author is from the standard citation; the full author list was not checked on the page.

lindsey-2025-introspection.title: Jack Lindsey, "Emergent Introspective Awareness in Large Language Models," Transformer Circuits Thread, 29 October 2025; also arXiv:2601.01828

consulted.copy: Web page; the abstract, introduction and caveats, quick tour, methods notes, and the beginning of the self-report section were read. The later sections did not load as text.

lindsey-2025-introspection.notes: Concept injection; all-caps "loudness or shouting" example; about 20% success for Opus 4.1 and 4 at the best layer and strength; 0 false positives over 100 control trials for production models; prefilled "bread" experiment (quick tour only); explicit caveats on unreliability and on not addressing subjective experience.

turpin-et-al-2023.title: Miles Turpin, Julian Michael, Ethan Perez, and Samuel R. Bowman, "Language Models Don't Always Say What They Think: Unfaithful Explanations in Chain-of-Thought Prompting," NeurIPS 2023; arXiv:2305.04388

consulted.copy: arXiv abstract page (v2, 9 December 2023)

turpin-et-al-2023.notes: Abstract: few-shot options reordered so the answer is always "(A)"; models systematically fail to mention this in explanations; accuracy drops by as much as 36% on 13 BIG-Bench Hard tasks; GPT-3.5 and Claude 1.0. The venue comes from the arXiv comments field and was not checked against the proceedings.

chen-et-al-2025.title: Yanda Chen et al. (Anthropic Alignment Science), "Reasoning Models Don't Always Say What They Think," Anthropic research summary, 3 April 2025

consulted.copy: Anthropic research summary page; the linked full PDF was not read

chen-et-al-2025.notes: Section "Testing for faithfulness": hints include a Stanford professor's answer and an "unauthorized access" message; averaged over hint types, Claude 3.7 Sonnet mentioned the hint 25% of the time and DeepSeek R1 39%. Lead author taken from the paper's standard citation; the author list was not checked on the page.

kepler-an-frisch.title: Johannes Kepler, Astronomia nova (1609), in Christian Frisch (ed.), Joannis Kepleri astronomi opera omnia, vol. 3 (Frankfurt and Erlangen, 1860)

consulted.copy: archive.org OCR text; passages located by Latin search and read in context

kepler-an-frisch.notes: The Latin quoted and translated in essay 002000. Frisch's page numbers differ from those of the Gesammelte Werke (KGW). Translations in the essay are the author's own and are literal.

kepler-an-1609.title: Johannes Kepler, Astronomia nova AITIOLOGETOS, seu physica coelestis (Heidelberg, 1609), first edition

consulted.copy: archive.org OCR text

kepler-an-1609.notes: Used to confirm the ch. 19 wording ('sola igitur haec octo minuta viam praeiverunt'). The parenthetical about errors of 30 minutes printed by Frisch is not in the 1609 main text.

gingerich-1972.title: Owen Gingerich, "Johannes Kepler and the New Astronomy," Quarterly Journal of the Royal Astronomical Society 13 (1972), pp. 346-373

consulted.copy: NASA ADS page images

gingerich-1972.notes: Source of the week-long wager anecdote (p. 353, unsourced there), the vicarious-hypothesis geometry (p. 351, Fig. 3), the 'scaffolding' contrast with Ptolemy and Copernicus (p. 351), the distance law (pp. 353-354), and KGW locators (ch. 19 = KGW 3, p. 178).

gingerich-dsb-kepler.title: Owen Gingerich, "Kepler, Johannes," Dictionary of Scientific Biography, vol. 7 (1973), PDF hosted by MacTutor

consulted.copy: PDF text; page numbers below are pages of the hosted PDF

gingerich-dsb-kepler.notes: Gingerich's translation of Kepler's 1595 account (19 July; triangles; the smaller circle; 'why have plane figures among three-dimensional orbits?'; the pleasure passage); fit within 5 percent except Jupiter; the Lutheran school in Graz; arrival at Benatky; Tycho's death on 24 October 1601 and deathbed wish; appointment within two days; Mars assigned to Kepler; 1621 edition with the text unchanged and new notes.

sep-kepler.title: Daniel A. Di Liscia, "Johannes Kepler," Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy (revised 14 September 2025)

consulted.copy: Web page, sections 3, 4.2, 4.4, and 5

sep-kepler.notes: Mysterium ch. 18 quoting Rheticus on Copernicus's view that exact agreement with imperfect data is unnecessary (§4.4); the 1621 footnote conceding that the eccentricities cannot be derived a priori (§3); polyhedra in Harmonices mundi Book 5 (§3); the second law found before the ellipse (§5). Its locator for the eight-minutes passage, 'KGW 3, p. 286', is Donahue's page, not KGW's.

mactutor-kepler.title: J. V. Field, "Johannes Kepler," MacTutor History of Mathematics (1999)

consulted.copy: Web page

mactutor-kepler.notes: Order of the nested solids; polyhedra 'still there' in the 1619 Harmony; the third-law passage quoted from the Aiton, Duncan and Field translation (Harmonice mundi Book 5, ch. 3, p. 411); Kepler sent the Mysterium to Tycho hoping better observations would improve the agreement.

mactutor-brahe.title: J. J. O'Connor and E. F. Robertson, "Tycho Brahe," MacTutor History of Mathematics (2003)

consulted.copy: Web page

mactutor-brahe.notes: Quotes Swerdlow's review of Wesley (1978): errors mostly 0.5' to 1.0', and 'Kepler's belief that Tycho's observations could be trusted to better than two minutes is amply confirmed.' Open-sighted instruments, with no telescope.

rice-brahe.title: Albert Van Helden, "Tycho Brahe," The Galileo Project, Rice University

consulted.copy: Web page

rice-brahe.notes: 'previous astronomers made observations accurate to perhaps 15 arc minutes, those of Tycho were accurate to perhaps 2 arc minutes ... his best observations were accurate to about half an arc minute.' The Tychonic system.

hellman-dsb-brahe.title: C. Doris Hellman, "Brahe, Tycho," Dictionary of Scientific Biography, vol. 2 (1970), PDF hosted by MacTutor

consulted.copy: PDF text

hellman-dsb-brahe.notes: Kepler arrived at Benatky on 3 February 1600; Mars was worked on by Longomontanus and turned over to Kepler; the Tychonic system (Earth at rest, Sun circling the Earth, planets circling the Sun); an illness of eleven days; the deathbed wish that the Rudolphine Tables follow the Tychonic system; large instruments.

dreyer-1890.title: J. L. E. Dreyer, Tycho Brahe: A Picture of Scientific Life and Work in the Sixteenth Century (Edinburgh, 1890)

consulted.copy: archive.org OCR text

dreyer-1890.notes: Prints Kepler's Latin entry in Tycho's observation log: 'Nocte, quam ultimam habuit, per delirium, quo omnia suavissima fuere, creberrime haec verba iteravit, quasi qui carmen texit. Ne frustra vixisse videar.'
